title: A Cipher for the Extraction
premise: Mirabel Marchetti, a UN-attached interpreter with a forged past and a packed go-bag, boards a peace flight to broker a ceasefire that powerful actors have already decided must fail. Mid-flight, every digital record of the aircraft vanishes — manifests, radar logs, passenger lists — and when it makes an emergency landing in a hostile border region, she realizes the disappearance was engineered by the same covert network that trained her years ago under another name. To survive, and to save the delegates the network intends to bury as casualties of a failed peace, Mirabel must turn her skills against her handlers: decoding their extraction protocols, recruiting the few people who trust her, and choosing between the duty she was conditioned to obey and the found family she never expected. The story ends with Mirabel broadcasting the network's own cipher to expose it, burning her old identity for good, and walking out of the wreckage not as an asset but as a witness — alive, implicated, and finally free.
about_author: Theo Voss is the pen name of a former humanitarian logistics coordinator who spent six years in conflict zones before turning to fiction full-time. Voss writes thrillers about people whose languages, loyalties, and identities are their most dangerous tools.

chapters.title: The Packed Bag
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In Geneva, she rehearses talking points for a doomed peace delegation while checking the go-bag she's kept ready for three years. A coded message from an unknown handler confirms the mission is compromised. Beat: dread disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She notices the passenger manifest contains names that shouldn't exist — including one from her buried past. She flags it quietly, telling no one. Beat: the first crack in her controlled world.

chapters.title: Wheels Up
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Mirabel and delegation lead Ambassador Okafor aboard the aircraft. Small human moments — a junior aide's jokes, Okafor's exhausted faith in the process. Beat: warmth established so it can be threatened.

chapters.title: Signal Loss
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Somewhere over the Adriatic, the plane's transponder dies; ground control has no record the flight exists. Passengers' phones go dark in unison. Beat: quiet horror as the world erases them.

chapters.title: The Language of Extraction
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She recognizes the blackout pattern — it matches protocols from a training program she survived under a different name. Flashback fragments surface. Beat: recognition and self-revulsion.

chapters.title: Forced Down
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The aircraft makes a hard emergency landing at a decommissioned airstrip in a contested border valley. Armed men in unmarked gear surround it. Beat: claustrophobic descent into danger.

chapters.title: Counting Heads
chapters.summary: Junior aide Tomas's POV. He organizes passengers while Mirabel negotiates with the soldiers in three languages, buying time. Beat: Tomas begins to see Mirabel isn't what she claims.

chapters.title: Handler's Voice
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV: Colonel Ives, running the operation remotely, orders witnesses minimized and the interpreter 'recovered intact.' Beat: cold institutional menace; Mirabel is cargo, not crew.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Opens
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Alone at night, she opens the bag: cash, false passports, a burner phone that rings with a voice from her training days. Beat: the lie she polished becomes a weapon she must aim at its makers.

chapters.title: Okafor's Doubt
chapters.summary: Ambassador Okafor's POV. He confronts Mirabel with what he overheard; she gives him half the truth. He chooses, provisionally, to trust her. Beat: love against duty begins — his duty to the mission, hers to survival.

chapters.title: First Blood
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. An escape attempt by two security officers ends in their deaths, staged to look like an accident. The survivors understand they're being culled. Beat: terror hardens into resolve.

chapters.title: Cipher in the Walls
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She finds the network's operational cipher embedded in the airstrip's decommissioned comms equipment — proof this site was built for exactly this. Beat: the conspiracy gains architecture.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Was Nadia
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, deep flashback. Her recruitment, training, and the night she walked away, leaving a sister-trainee behind. Beat: guilt revealed as the engine of her justice.

chapters.title: Allies Among Hostages
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Mirabel quietly recruits Tomas, Okafor, and flight engineer Riva. Each brings a skill; each takes a risk. Beat: found family assembling under fire.

chapters.title: Ives Arrives
chapters.summary: Colonel Ives lands in person, charming and surgical. He greets Mirabel by her old name. Beat: the mask drops publicly; now everyone knows she was theirs.

chapters.title: Betrayal Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Shaken, he weighs exposing Mirabel against using her knowledge. Their confrontation turns intimate — two liars recognizing each other. Beat: love against duty sharpens.

chapters.title: The Extraction List
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She decodes the cipher enough to learn the plan: delegates die in a staged militant attack; Mirabel is extracted and re-indoctrinated. Beat: stakes made explicit and personal.

chapters.title: Riva's Wire
chapters.summary: Flight engineer Riva's POV. She splices a hidden antenna to the downed aircraft's emergency beacon, sending a burst transmission no one expects. Beat: hope through technical defiance.

chapters.title: Answer From Nowhere
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The beacon gets a reply — from the sister-trainee she abandoned, now embedded in the network and watching Ives. Beat: the past offers a hand instead of a knife.

chapters.title: Terms of Treason
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Mirabel and the sister, Lena, via coded messages. Lena will help if Mirabel proves she'll burn the whole network, not just escape. Beat: alliance built on mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Massacre
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The captors stage-drill a 'militant assault,' and Tomas maps the choreography, realizing the date is tomorrow. Beat: countdown pressure begins.

chapters.title: What Mirabel Steals
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She lifts Ives's field tablet during a staged negotiation, copying the full extraction protocol. Nearly caught; saved by Okafor's improvisation. Beat: partnership cemented in risk.

chapters.title: The Decryption Night
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Riva's POV. Working by generator light, they crack the tablet's cipher layer by layer. Mirabel recognizes her own training fingerprints in the code. Beat: intimacy of shared work; grief for who she was.

chapters.title: Lena's Price
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Inside the network, she sabotages a supply run to buy the hostages a day, knowing discovery means death. Beat: sacrifice foreshadowed; loyalty tested.

chapters.title: Okafor's Choice
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Offered release if he disavows the ceasefire and signs a statement blaming militants, he refuses on record. Beat: duty redefined — integrity over survival.

chapters.title: Storm Cover
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. A storm grounds Ives's extraction aircraft, delaying everything. The group uses the hours to prepare a counter-plan: seize the comms bunker. Beat: breath before the plunge.

chapters.title: The Bunker Job
chapters.summary: Mirabel, Tomas, and Riva infiltrate the comms bunker during shift change. Tense, near-silent sequence. Beat: competence as catharsis.

chapters.title: Lena Exposed
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Ives discovers her sabotage. Interrogated, she gives nothing but buys a final message to Mirabel: coordinates and a warning. Beat: heartbreak as fuel.

chapters.title: Broadcast Position
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. From the bunker she can transmit the decrypted evidence globally — but only by revealing the site's location, inviting a strike that could kill the hostages. Beat: impossible arithmetic.

chapters.title: Ives's Offer
chapters.summary: Ives and Mirabel face to face. He offers her old life back: name restored, sister spared, hostages framed posthumously. Beat: temptation rendered sincerely; the devil argues well.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She declines in four languages, deliberately, so witnesses hear. Ives orders the assault moved up to tonight. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The group races to move hostages to cover positions before the staged attack. Tomas is wounded shielding others. Beat: found family bleeding together.

chapters.title: Transmission
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She broadcasts the cipher-decrypted evidence, naming the network, the flight, and herself — including her crimes. Beat: justice outside the law, paid for with her own exposure.

chapters.title: The Assault
chapters.summary: Action ensemble POV. The staged militant attack goes live against prepared defenders. Riva holds the bunker; Okafor refuses to leave the wounded. Beat: chaos met with chosen courage.

chapters.title: Sisters
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Lena's POV. Lena breaks free during the chaos; the sisters fight side by side for the first time. Lena takes a fatal wound covering Mirabel's retreat. Beat: love arriving exactly too late.

chapters.title: Ives Falls
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Cornered in the bunker, Ives offers one last deal; Mirabel answers with the recording of his own orders, already uploaded. His masters silence him before capture. Beat: the machine eats its own.

chapters.title: Dawn Count
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Survivors count themselves in the grey morning light. News outlets worldwide carry the leaked files. Beat: exhaustion edged with disbelief — they're still here.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In a safehouse hearing, she testifies fully, surrendering her false identities and accepting investigation. Okafor stands as her character witness. Beat: accountability chosen, not imposed.

chapters.title: The Unpacked Bag
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Months later, she unpacks the go-bag item by item, keeping only Lena's photograph. Okafor visits; something unhurried begins. Beat: grief and tenderness coexisting.

chapters.title: A Cipher for the Living
chapters.summary: Final ensemble POV. The surviving delegates reconvene the talks that were meant to fail — and this time they hold. Mirabel interprets, openly, under her real name. Beat: peace as the answer to violence; identity reclaimed.
